about.title: South El Monte Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases carry unique legal hurdles in California, and South El Monte residents facing a suspected error at a local clinic or hospital deserve clear guidance. Whether the issue involved a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error, these cases require careful review of medical records and, in most instances, a qualified expert to establish that the standard of care was not met. LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured patients and families with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain the realistic path forward. Timing matters in these cases because California law sets specific windows for filing and requires advance notice before a lawsuit can even begin. Rather than trying to sort through medical jargon and legal deadlines alone, South El Monte residents can use our service to get matched with someone who regularly handles these claims and can walk through the details with you directly.

items.title: Deadlines Are Strict and Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, but never more than three years from the injury itself. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before any malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the healthcare provider must receive written notice 90 days in advance. Missing this step can delay or jeopardize a claim, so early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove malpractice — California law typically requires a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached. The attorney you're matched with can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in South El Monte?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it occurred, whichever comes first. These deadlines can be confusing, so it's worth having an attorney review your specific timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: Is a poor medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law recognizes that not every bad result means a doctor did something wrong. Malpractice requires showing the provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care, which is why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate the case.
